reviews.review: Great game getting a third year of content. One of the best Warhammer 40k games to ever come out. A little shady with the DLC but they fixed it so that's good.

Trying to be harsher and more honest in my reviews, and honestly. Space Marine 2 is a game I have a lot of gripes with. Primarily, that for a PvE focused game, having thirteen missions total after three years is horrendously inadequate, and there kind of isn't an excuse for it. Space Marine as a game *should* be a power fantasy with some skill expression (particularly from the melee combat), but instead Saber have taken the entirety of Arrowhead's book and built everything around catering to the hardcore sweat crowd, which sucks when you want to just chill out and kill some things. The game is boring when played below Substantial difficulty, and above Resolute it becomes unfair to play unless you're actively co-ordinating with friends on discord or whatever. The Thousand Sons in particular can be so unfun to fight its been a meme in the community that you just don't play their missions for years. They also seem to have taken Arrowhead's book on balancing, because so many decisions are just ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ weird. Assault in particular feels like ♥♥♥♥ to play and his jumppack barely gets him three meters in the air in PvE. Special variants of weapons that you have to do some short grinding to unlock sometimes just launch utterly ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and useless. Seige mode just isn't a fun take on a wave defence mode IMO, and PvP has been essentially abandoned since the game launched, which is saying something because a. The main game has had barely any new missions added, and b. The PvP would be pretty fun if it wasn't completely dead. There are 101 little gripes with the customisation system that make it overall disappointing. A surprising and frustrating amount of good customisations pieces are locked behind grinding the highest difficulties, which as previously mentioned, is unfun unless you want to play this game as something to really have to lock in for.

Overall, the more I play it, the more Space Marine 2 feels like a shell with very little actually in it. If you don't have friends that want to commit to playing it regularly, don't buy it.
